```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(marea)
library(stars)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
```

## Introduction

In this vignette, we will demonstrate how to access and manipulate spatial objects from the `marea` package. While spatial data can also be stored as `sf` or `spatRaster` objects in `marea`, the two datasets provided by default are `stars` objects for stable saving and manipulation. Here, we demonstrate how to access, subset by spatial or temporal dimensions, and visualize spatial data.

## Upload Spatial Data

```{r}
data("satellite_ocean_colour")
ea.summary(satellite_ocean_colour)
```

The `satellite_ocean_colour` dataset features gridded data for five variables related to algal blooms in the Northwest Atlantic. By default, the `stars` data object features data from 341 longitudes, 270 latitudes, and 28 timesteps (here, years).

```{r, warning=FALSE}
plot(satellite_ocean_colour["t_start_value"], style = "fill",) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(fill = "t_start")
```

## Subset by Dimensions

`ea.subset.spatial.dims()` allows filtration of data by spatial and temporal dimensions: latitude, longitude, year, and -- when applicable -- month. For example, to subset an `ea_spatial` object to a specificed latitudinal and longitudinal range at only select years, we could use:

### Specify Dimensions

```{r, warning=FALSE}
satellite_ocean_colour_2 <- ea.subset.spatial.dims(satellite_ocean_colour,
                                                   lat_range = c(37,46),
                                                   lon_range = c(-65,-55),
                                                   years = c(2015, 2020, 2025))

plot(satellite_ocean_colour_2, style = "fill",
     value_col = "amplitude_real_value") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(fill = "amplitude")
```

### Specify Shape

The same function allows us to subset spatially to a region of focus using th input of an external `sf` spatial shape. Below, we show filtration to the lobster fishing area 33 from the `Mar.data` package.

```{r, warning=FALSE}

# get sf shape from Mar.data package:

library(Mar.data) # available from https://github.com/PopulationEcologyDivision/Mar.data

data("LFAs_sf")

lfa_33 <- LFAs_sf %>%
  filter(LFA == "33") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(satellite_ocean_colour@data)) # use same CRS as the data for spatial operations


# subset to LFA 33 shape
satellite_ocean_colour_3 <- ea.subset.spatial.dims(satellite_ocean_colour,
                                                   shape = lfa_33,
                                                   years = c(2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2025))

# plot
plot(satellite_ocean_colour_3, style = "fill", value_col = "amplitude_real_value") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(fill = "amplitude") + 
  geom_sf(data = lfa_33, 
          color = "red",
          fill = "transparent",
          linewidth = 1)
```

### Subset by Values

In other cases, we might want to subset by the values of one or more variables in the dataset, as opposed to attributes, in which case we use `ea.subset.spatial.values()`. This functiion masks all variables in the dataset by values of the selected variable.

```{r, warning=FALSE}

satellite_ocean_colour_4 <- ea.subset.spatial.values(satellite_ocean_colour_3,
                                                   variable = "t_start_value",
                                                   value_range = c(1,70))


plot(satellite_ocean_colour_4, style = "fill", value_col = "amplitude_real_value") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(fill = "amplitude") + 
  geom_sf(data = lfa_33, 
          color = "red",
          fill = "transparent",
          linewidth = 1) + 
  facet_wrap(~time)
```

### Contour Plots

Default marea spatial plotting funcitons allow for style 'contour', which creates sf shapes around contours of spatial data values. Contour plots can be either of two `contour.time` values: "aggregate", for contours of mean values across timesteps, or "timestep" for contoours within each time layer.

Example 1: average temperature bands

```{r, warning=FALSE}

data("glorys_bottom_temperature")
plot(glorys_bottom_temperature, style = "contour", contour.time = "aggregate")

```

Example 2: July temperature bands in LFA33

```{r, warning=FALSE}

# subset to july within LFA33
glorys_sub <- ea.subset.spatial.dims(
  glorys_bottom_temperature,
  years = seq(2016, 2026, by = 2),
  months = 7,
  shape = lfa_33
)

plot(glorys_sub, style = "contour", contour.time = "timestep") +
  # add shape
  geom_sf(data = lfa_33, color = "red", fill = "transparent") +
  # facet by timestep
  facet_wrap(~time) +
  labs(fill = "July Bottom Temperature") 

```

## Saving marea spatial

`marea` sptaial functions are compatible with spatial data in multiple formats for intermediate object creation and manipulation: `sf`, `spatRaster`, and `stars`. But saving data in `marea` is most compatible with `stars` data. For example, spatial obejcts saved to the disk (or in the package) through `terraa` require external C++ pointer referece objects, which disconnect from their sources when using `save.rds()` or `save.rda()`. A solution to this issue is using `terra::wrap()` before saving, and `terra::unwrap()` after loading, whereas `stars` or `sf` objects are directly loadable.
